issues.claim: "different service lines arrive through it into one general inbox" (section 1, "Now")
issues.problem: Stated as fact. The form's delivery address cannot be observed; what is verifiable is that there is one form, no service field, and only one published general inbox (info@distinctengineering.com). The routing conclusion is a strong inference from those facts, not a directly sourced statement.
issues.fix: Reword to the observable fact, e.g. "one form with no service field, and a single general inbox published on the page" (or mark it as an inference).

issues.claim: Section 2 impact: "250 working days x 2-3 hours a day x 30% automated"
issues.problem: Internally consistent and clearly labelled as an assumption, but it does not match the researcher's own analysis.json (which assumed about 1-1.6 hrs/day of scheduling and report chasing at 25-40% automation). The audit's baseline is roughly double, so the range is lower than the analysis figure but built on a different, unexplained assumption.
issues.fix: Either use the analysis assumption (1-1.6 hrs/day) or note that 2-3 hrs/day is a fresh assumption; keep the decimal-hours phrasing so the reader can test it.

issues.claim: Impact headline ranges (e.g. "= about $1,434-$2,869 a year")
issues.problem: The headline ranges are computed with the 1.25 benefits-loaded rate ($28.69), not the $22.95 base rate quoted first. A reader who multiplies 50-100 hours by $22.95 gets a lower figure and may read the range as inflated.
issues.fix: State the rate used for the headline range, e.g. "= about $1,434-$2,869 a year at the loaded rate".

issues.problem: Accurate, but the page that carries it (corporate-summary) is not in the Sources list, so the claim is untraceable from the document alone. Same for the lab accreditation, which is only partly covered by the qualifications link.
issues.fix: Add https://distinct-esi.com/corporate-summary/ to Sources; optionally cite the qualifications page for the AASHTO/A2LA lab accreditation explicitly.

issues.problem: No published source exists for either volume; they are unlabelled inputs rather than sourced figures. The audit's own caveat ("Estimates are illustrative") covers this, but the volume figures sit outside the parentheses that say "our assumption".
issues.fix: Mark the volume itself as an assumption, e.g. "(assumed 100-200 enquiries a year, our assumption)".

issues.problem: The audit names the firm correctly but never states that it is in North Brunswick, NJ or that its site shows no street address. Nothing wrong is said; the location is simply absent, which weakens the walk-in opener.
issues.fix: Add "North Brunswick, NJ" to the title or opening line (confirmed by corporate-summary and the PERM postings page).
